code_actions.rationale: Cardiac arrest documented on ICU day 4 (post-admission); POA should be 'N'.
Post-operative complication coding supported by post-op course; retained as complication-of-procedure documentation.
Superficial sternal wound infection after surgery is documented (MSSA) and justifies an infection-following-procedure code.

Facesheet and discharge documentation indicate full-code status and the discharge/transfer summary does not document Do-Not-Resuscitate; Z66 (Do not resuscitate) is not supported by the chart documentation.
No provider documentation of ESRD or CKD stage 5; nephrology documents contrast-induced AKI with recovery and no RRT. I12.0 (hypertensive CKD stage 5/ESRD) is not supported.

Provider-authored diagnosis of 'sepsis' is not present in the chart or discharge problem list; the record documents a localized post-operative MSSA sternal wound infection but no documented sepsis syndrome meeting the policy requirement for A41.9 as coded.

evidence.quote: Assessment 62-year-old man with acute anterior ST-elevation myocardial infarction complicated by cardiogenic shock requiring mechanical circulatory support, acute kidney injury from contrast and shock, and pulmonary edema requiring intubation.

Assessment Acute anterior STEMI with hemodynamic collapse. TIMI 2 flow post-PCI to proximal LAD; residual multivessel disease in circumflex and RCA territories. Cardiogenic shock requiring Impella CP and IABP support.
ABG pH 7.28 / PaCO2 34 / PaO2 62 on NRB 15L.

After multidisciplinary heart-team evaluation, emergency 3-vessel coronary artery bypass grafting (LIMA to LAD, SVG to OM1 and RCA) was performed on ICU day 7 with difficult wean from cardiopulmonary bypass.

The post-operative course was complicated by post-cardiotomy hypotension requiring transfusion, failed extubation from flash pulmonary edema with reintubation on ICU day 11, new-onset atrial fibrillation post-cardiotomy controlled with amiodarone, a superficial sternal wound infection with methicillin-susceptible S. aureus treated with cefazolin and wound VAC therapy, catheter-associated right popliteal DVT treated with therapeutic anticoagulation, and profound ICU-acquired weakness.

Consultation requested by the primary care team. Chart reviewed and patient examined at the bedside. KDIGO stage 2 AKI from iodinated contrast exposure in setting of cardiogenic shock and poor perfusion. Creatinine peak 2.8; oliguric with adequate response to careful diuresis.

CBC: WBC 6.0 x103/uL, Hgb 9.8 g/dL, Hct 29%, platelets 233 x109/L (neutrophils 73%). BMP: Na 138, K 4.2, Cl 103, CO2 25, BUN 27, creatinine 1.11 mg/dL, glucose 146 mg/dL, Ca 8.5, Mg 1.9, Phos 3.6. ABG (07:00): pH 7.37 / PaCO2 35 / PaO2 90 / HCO3 23; lactate 0.9 mmol/L; P/F ratio 305.

The course was complicated by contrast-induced acute kidney injury (KDIGO 2, non-dialysis), pulseless ventricular tachycardia arrest on ICU day 4 with successful ROSC after 8 minutes of ACLS and targeted temperature management, and cardiogenic shock refractory to medical therapy.

Discharge / Transfer Diagnoses Resolved acute anterior STEMI status post primary PCI to LAD and emergency 3-vessel CABG; heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (EF 35-40%); resolved cardiogenic shock; resolved post-cardiac-arrest state with intact neurologic function; resolved post-cardiotomy atrial fibrillation; contrast-induced AKI with renal recovery; superficial sternal wound infection (MSSA) on cefazolin with wound VAC; right popliteal DVT on apixaban; type 2 diabetes mellitus; hypertension; hyperlipidemia; ICU-acquired weakness.

Admission Orders Admit: CVICU. Condition: critical. Vitals: continuous telemetry with 12-lead capability, arterial-line BP, SpO2, PA catheter monitoring; hourly assessment; strict I/O. Ventilation: lung-protective settings post-intubation; wean as tolerated. Hemodynamics: norepinephrine to MAP ≥ 65; dobutamine 2-10 mcg/kg/min for cardiac index ≥ 2.2; Impella CP set at P-8; IABP 1:1 with augmentation; ScvO2 goal > 65%.

The course was complicated by contrast-induced acute kidney injury (KDIGO 2, non-dialysis), pulseless ventricular tachycardia arrest on ICU day 4 with successful ROSC after 8 minutes of ACLS and targeted temperature management, and cardiogenic shock refractory to medical therapy.

Past Medical / Surgical History Medical: Hypertension (approximately 15 years), hyperlipidemia, type 2 diabetes mellitus (A1c 7.8% approximately 6 months prior), tobacco use (former 20 pack-year smoker, quit 3 years ago), family history of premature coronary artery disease (father MI age 55).

Laboratory Data Troponin I 32.4 ng/mL (peak); CK-MB 145 U/L; WBC 14.2; Hgb 13.1; platelets 245; Na 136, K 4.3, Cl 102, CO2 22, BUN 28, creatinine 1.4 mg/dL (baseline 0.9); glucose 268; lactate 4.8 mmol/L; BNP 4200 pg/mL; INR 1.1.

system_note: Audit summary and line-by-line determination for claim MR_10 (admit 2026-04-15 -> discharge 2026-08-15). I reviewed the billed diagnosis and procedure lines against the medical record notes and the governing DRG policies retrieved for cardiogenic shock, acute respiratory failure, AKI and sepsis. Key facts from the record that drive the determination: 1) Principal diagnosis (I21.09) - supported as principal. The admitting H&P and discharge/transfer documentation state acute anterior ST-elevation MI as the reason for admission and the team performed urgent coronary reperfusion and later emergency CABG (principal diagnosis sequencing is correct). Evidence: H&P assessment documents acute anterior STEMI with cardiogenic shock (NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_10.pdf-n9, History & Physical, p.668) and the operative/transfer course documents emergency 3-vessel CABG (NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_10.pdf-n1052, Discharge / Transfer Summary, p.936). See evidence_cited ev_0001 and ev_0004. 2) Cardiogenic shock (R57.0) - supported; meets the policy's documentation + device/management presumption. The record documents cardiogenic shock on admission, persistent hemodynamic instability, and placement of mechanical circulatory support (Impella CP and IABP). Per the cardiogenic shock policy, placement of MCS with provider attribution satisfies Criterion 2 for R57.0. Evidence: H&P and Interventional note (NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_10.pdf-n9, H&P, p.668; NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_10.pdf-n12, Interventional Cardiology Consultation, p.568) (ev_0001, ev_0002). 3) Acute respiratory failure (J96.01) - supported and documented on admission with objective hypoxemia and escalation to invasive ventilation. Admission ABG shows PaO2 62 on high-flow NRB and the record documents intubation for pulmonary edema; the presumption rule for invasive ventilation supports J96.01 even if a pre-intubation room-air ABG is unavailable. Evidence: ABG on admission (PaO2 62) (NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_10.pdf-n9, H&P, p.668) and the discharge note describing intubation and subsequent failed extubation/reintubation (NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_10.pdf-n1052, Discharge / Transfer Summary, p.936) (ev_0003, ev_0005). 4) Cardiac arrest (I46.9) - supported as a diagnosis but POA flag is incorrect on the billed claim. The medical record documents a pulseless ventricular tachycardia arrest that occurred on ICU day 4 (i.e., after admission), not present on arrival; therefore the POA indicator for I46.9 should be N, not Y. Evidence: discharge hospital course documenting pulseless ventricular tachycardia arrest on ICU day 4 with ROSC (NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_10.pdf-n1052, Discharge / Transfer Summary, p.936) (ev_0011). 5) Acute kidney injury (N17.9) - supported as an acute, post-contrast AKI (KDIGO stage 2) in the setting of cardiogenic shock, documented by nephrology; POA=N is correct. Nephrology documents contrast-induced KDIGO stage 2 AKI with creatinine peak ~2.8 and oliguric interval; discharge labs show renal recovery (creatinine 1.11 mg/dL). Per the AKI policy, this meets the Medical/Surgical and Acute-on-Chronic pathways when documented and substantiated by KDIGO criteria and nephrology assessment. Evidence: Nephrology consultation (KDIGO stage 2 AKI, creatinine peak 2.8) and discharge BMP showing creatinine 1.11 mg/dL (NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_10.pdf-n30, Nephrology Consultation, p.351; NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_10.pdf-n1052, Discharge / Transfer Summary, p.936) (ev_0006, ev_0007). 6) Sepsis (A41.9) - NOT supported as billed. The DRG sepsis policy requires provider documentation of sepsis (or clear objective criteria plus provider attribution) to code A41.9/A40.-. In this record I found documentation of a superficial sternal wound infection due to MSSA treated with cefazolin and a wound VAC, but I did not find a provider-authored diagnosis line explicitly documenting 'sepsis' as a confirmed diagnosis in the notes or the discharge/transfer diagnosis list. The discharge/transfer diagnoses enumerate wound infection, DVT, AKI, cardiogenic shock and related problems but do not list 'sepsis' as a discharge diagnosis; because policy requires provider documentation (or the sepsis clinical pathways with vasopressor + lactate etc.), A41.9 as billed (POA=Y, MCC) is not supported and is removed. Evidence: discharge/transfer summary problem list and the wound-infection description (NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_10.pdf-n1052, Discharge / Transfer Summary, p.936; NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_10.pdf-n1052, Discharge / Transfer Summary, p.936) (ev_0004). Note: there are antibiotic/education notes that reference 'sepsis' in lay terms (patient education) but those do not substitute for provider diagnosis documentation per policy. 7) Hypertensive CKD with ESRD (I12.0) - NOT supported. The record documents a contrast-induced AKI with recovery and nephrology explicitly anticipating recovery without RRT; there is no supporting provider documentation of stage 5 CKD/ESRD requiring I12.0. Discharge labs show creatinine recovery (creatinine 1.11 mg/dL). Per the AKI policy and Excludes1 rules, N17.x and N18.6 (ESRD) cannot be coded together without explicit documentation. I12.0 (hypertensive CKD stage 5/ESRD) is therefore not supported and is removed. Evidence: Nephrology consult documenting contrast-induced KDIGO 2 AKI, creatinine trends and recovery, and discharge BMP with creatinine 1.11 mg/dL (NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_10.pdf-n30, Nephrology Consultation, p.351; NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_10.pdf-n1052, Discharge / Transfer Summary, p.936) (ev_0006, ev_0007). 8) Procedure coding and laterality conflict (06BQ0ZZ) - human escalation required. The claim contains ICD-10-PCS 06BQ0ZZ (Excision of right saphenous vein, open approach). The operative/procedure narrative(s) retrieved include explicit language that a saphenous vein was harvested from the left leg for SVGs (see the operative/procedure note excerpts in the retrieval transcript). The dataset's conflict-tracking flags these particular procedure-note passages as a record_vs_claim conflict (/ ), indicating the record and the billed line cannot both be correct and the record does not settle which is right. Because laterality drives ICD-10-PCS assignment and the record passages conflict, this specific procedure line needs human review to resolve laterality. I therefore mark the claim Finding and request HITL for the 06BQ0ZZ laterality. Evidence: discharge summary documents 3-vessel CABG with SVGs (NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_10.pdf-n1052, Discharge / Transfer Summary, p.936) and the separate procedure note(s) (conflicted) describing left-leg harvest (NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_10.pdf-n60 / NOTE-Readmission-RM_10-index-MR_10.pdf-n55 - flagged in the conflict list). See hitl_question for details. Net effect and corrective actions taken in this audit (claim-level): - Removed I12.0 (hypertensive CKD stage 5 / ESRD) - unsupported; evidence shows contrast-induced AKI with recovery and no RRT (ev_0006, ev_0007). - Removed A41.9 (sepsis, unspecified) - no provider-authored sepsis diagnosis found in the chart or discharge problem list; only wound infection (MSSA) documented (ev_0004). If the provider has separate documentation explicitly diagnosing sepsis (with vasopressor/lactate or statement 'sepsis'), supply it for reconsideration. - Changed POA for I46.9 (cardiac arrest) from Y to N - arrest occurred on ICU day 4 per hospital course (ev_0011). - Left all other billed diagnoses and procedures in place pending resolution of the laterality conflict for saphenous vein excision (06BQ0ZZ) - see HITL request. Supported high-severity MCC diagnoses (R57.0, J96.01, I50.23) remain billed because provider documentation and objective data or device placement meet the policy validation criteria (ev_0001, ev_0002, ev_0003, ev_0010). Documents and quotations relied upon (see evidence_cited entries below) - cited passages are from: H&P (NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_10.pdf-n9, p.668), Interventional Cardiology consult (NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_10.pdf-n12, p.568), Nephrology consult (NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_10.pdf-n30, p.351), and Discharge / Transfer Summary (NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_10.pdf-n1052, pp.936-937) among others. The cardiogenic shock and respiratory-failure policies were applied as retrieved during the review (policy rule excerpts for R57.0 and J96.01 guided the validation criteria used above). Reviewer conclusion: Finding. The claim contains unsupported/miscoded diagnoses (I12.0 and A41.9 removed) and an incorrect POA flag (I46.9 changed to POA=N). Additionally, a procedure-laterality conflict for 06BQ0ZZ requires human resolution before final procedural coding can be certified. See code_decisions, revised_diagnosis_set, revised_procedure_set and hitl_question for specifics.
rationale_letter: To: Coding and Medical Records Department Re: Audit determination - Inpatient claim MR_10 (Admit 04/15/2026 - Discharge 08/15/2026) We audited the full DRG-level coding for the above inpatient stay against the medical record and applicable DRG validation criteria. After review, we find the claim contains multiple supported high-severity diagnoses (acute anterior STEMI, cardiogenic shock, acute respiratory failure, AKI, cardiac arrest, post-operative complications) but also contains diagnostic entries that are not supported by the provider documentation and at least one POA flag that is incorrect. The audit changes are listed below with the factual basis. Audit findings and corrections made: 1) I21.09 (ST-elevation myocardial infarction) - retained and remains the principal diagnosis. The H&P and discharge/transfer summary document acute anterior STEMI as the reason for admission and subsequent emergency CABG (source: H&P 04/15/2026 and Discharge/Transfer Summary, Dr. Menon) (supporting documentation available in the chart). 2) R57.0 (Cardiogenic shock) - retained (MCC). Provider documentation and placement of mechanical circulatory support (Impella CP and IABP) for cardiogenic shock satisfy the policy validation criteria for cardiogenic shock (policy presumption rule for MCS placement) and justify MCC assignment. 3) J96.01 (Acute respiratory failure with hypoxia) - retained (MCC). Objective hypoxemia and initiation of invasive ventilation are documented; the clinical intervention requirements for validation are met. 4) I46.9 (Cardiac arrest) - retained but POA changed to N. The chart documents pulseless VT arrest on ICU day 4 with ROSC; this event occurred after admission and therefore should not be indicated Present-on-Admission (POA=Y). The POA indicator on the submitted claim is incorrect. 5) N17.9 (Acute kidney failure) - retained (CC) with POA=N. Nephrology documents KDIGO stage 2 post-contrast AKI with a creatinine peak and subsequent recovery; acute AKI coding is supported. 6) A41.9 (Sepsis, unspecified organism) - REMOVED. The DRG sepsis policy requires explicit provider documentation of sepsis or the combination of specific sepsis criteria with provider attribution. The chart documents a superficial sternal wound infection due to MSSA and antibiotic therapy, but I found no provider-authored documentation of 'sepsis' as a confirmed diagnosis in the progress notes or discharge/transfer problem list. Without provider documentation or clear septic-shock criteria attributed to infection in the chart, A41.9 is not supported and is removed from the claim. If the provider can supply contemporaneous documentation explicitly diagnosing sepsis (or documentation of vasopressor-dependent shock + lactate >2 attributed to infection), we will re-evaluate. 7) I12.0 (Hypertensive CKD with stage 5 CKD / ESRD) - REMOVED. The nephrology consult and discharge labs document a contrast-induced AKI with recovery and state no RRT was anticipated; there is no evidence of ESRD or documented stage 5 CKD in the record to justify I12.0. Accordingly, I12.0 is not supportable for this encounter and is removed. 8) Procedure-laterality conflict (06BQ0ZZ - excision of right saphenous vein): The operative/procedure documentation retrieved in the chart contains conflicting laterality statements relative to the billed code (notes describing left-leg SVG harvest vs. a claim line for right saphenous excision). Because laterality is determinative for ICD-10-PCS assignment and the record contains a documented conflict that the automated review cannot resolve, this item is referred for human review. Please reconcile the operative note(s) and supply the final operative record specifying the harvested vein laterality so we can finalize the ICD-10-PCS assignment for the saphenous-vein harvest procedure. Corrective action requested from provider / coding team: - Confirm and provide any provider-authored documentation that explicitly diagnoses sepsis (or confirm absence). If sepsis was documented, provide the note(s) so A41.9 can be reinstated if supported. - Confirm whether the patient has ESRD or documented CKD stage 5 that was present on admission; if so, provide documentation. Otherwise I12.0 will remain removed. - Reconcile the operative/procedure documentation to confirm which saphenous vein (right vs left) was harvested for SVG grafting so the PCS procedure can be coded to the correct laterality. Enclosed: (1) The audit's revised diagnosis list and procedure list; (2) evidence citations from the chart used to support each correction. Sincerely, Senior Clinical Claims Auditor
